headline_marked: [[Apple files 'shocking evidence']] against ex-employee accused of stealing data for OpenAI
headline: Apple files 'shocking evidence' against ex-employee accused of stealing data for OpenAI
summary: Apple alleges former employee Chang Liu used a confidential circuit schematic and internal tool at OpenAI, and tried to destroy evidence, bolstering its trade secret theft lawsuit.
details: In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple has filed what it calls "shocking evidence" to support allegations that former employee Chang Liu stole trade secrets for OpenAI's benefit. These details emerged after Liu's old Apple work laptop was handed over for investigation.

Apple now alleges Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic and a tool sharing a name with an internal Apple engineering application in his work at OpenAI. The company also claims Liu enlisted an OpenAI colleague to help destroy evidence when he learned of Apple's investigation.

The filing states the MacBook evidence shows Apple's trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed, countering claims of "fishing expeditions." Apple further alleges OpenAI was "well-aware" of Liu's access to Apple data.
Previous filings included text messages from Liu, punctuated with "crying laughing" emojis, indicating his awareness of continued access to Apple files after his departure.

OpenAI previously defended Liu, stating he only accessed Apple files post-employment to assist former colleagues. They attributed this to Apple's failure to properly manage system access for departing employees.
However, Apple counters that Liu maintained access by exploiting a "rare, previously unknown authentication bug." TechCrunch has sought comment from OpenAI on these new allegations.

Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction to block OpenAI from working on hardware based on Apple's technology during the case. They also request expedited discovery, alleging more former employees may be implicated.
According to Apple's initial filing, over 400 former Apple employees are currently working at OpenAI.

Apple claims "shocking evidence" proves a former employee stole trade secrets for OpenAI. The tech giant alleges confidential schematics were used and evidence was destroyed.

In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple has filed what it calls "shocking evidence" to support allegations that former employee Chang Liu stole trade secrets for OpenAI's benefit. These details emerged after Liu's old Apple work laptop was handed over for investigation.

Apple now alleges Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic and a tool sharing a name with an internal Apple engineering application in his work at OpenAI. The company also claims Liu enlisted an OpenAI colleague to help destroy evidence when he learned of Apple's investigation.

The filing states the MacBook evidence shows Apple's trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed, countering claims of "fishing expeditions." Apple further alleges OpenAI was "well-aware" of Liu's access to Apple data.

Previous filings included text messages from Liu, punctuated with "crying laughing" emojis, indicating his awareness of continued access to Apple files after his departure.

OpenAI previously defended Liu, stating he only accessed Apple files post-employment to assist former colleagues. They attributed this to Apple's failure to properly manage system access for departing employees.

However, Apple counters that Liu maintained access by exploiting a "rare, previously unknown authentication bug." TechCrunch has sought comment from OpenAI on these new allegations.

Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction to block OpenAI from working on hardware based on Apple's technology during the case. They also request expedited discovery, alleging more former employees may be implicated.

According to Apple's initial filing, over 400 former Apple employees are currently working at OpenAI.
